videos.script: Lesson 1's loop could apply, and nothing else. It could not delete, it could not report, and it held the keys to everything. {{loop}} Argo CD is that loop, built properly. You install it from one pinned file and give it a read-only key to the repository. {{install}} Then you describe one Application. It says: this path of this repository belongs in this namespace. Argo CD compares the two and tells you two separate things. Is the cluster what Git says? And is it working? {{status}} Next you turn on automation. A merge reaches the cluster on its own. An object deleted from Git is deleted from the cluster. A change made by hand is undone in seconds. {{auto}} You also meet the cases where that is wrong, and how to tell Argo CD to leave one field alone. {{ignore}} Last, the Application itself moves into Git, and a project limits what any Application may touch. {{root}}
